evidence.detail: Cross Venue Net Arbitrage requires validation of assumed net_edge_bps against real chain-specific fees and slippage.

proposals.expected_effect: Quantified latency-driven slippage costs and realistic execution failure rates before canary promotion.
proposals.rationale: Arbitrage strategies are highly sensitive to latency and execution costs. Without runtime forensics, we must validate whether the expected net edge survives actual chain conditions, particularly Solana priority fees and EVM gas dynamics.
proposals.shadow_test: Simulate trades over a 24h window recording quoted vs. realised outcomes to measure deviation and execution failure rate. Stop if deviation > 50%.

proposals.downside_risk: Replicating stale routes could lead to systematic adverse selection and net losses.

evidence.detail: learned_route_replication logic depends on historical net positive average.

proposals.expected_effect: Determines if route replication has persistent forward edge or is purely a historical artifact.
proposals.rationale: Copying historical routes risks decay as market participants adapt. We need to shadow test if the historical average net bps persists in forward (out-of-sample) testing.
proposals.shadow_test: Record shadow replication of historical routes and measure net edge after actual observed gas fees over a 3-day window. Abort if net edge goes negative.

proposals.downside_risk: Model overfitting leading to false positives and eroded capital in live environments.
